chunks: And Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who said to another man, 'O son of the adulteress,' meaning adultery. He (as) said: 'If his mother is alive and present, and she comes forward to claim her right, he is to be flogged eighty lashes. And if she is absent, he is to be delayed until she arrives and claims her right. And if she has passed away and nothing is known of her except goodness, the one who falsely accused her is to be given the legal punishment - eighty lashes.'

key_terms.الْفَاعِلَةِ: The female doer (of an act), here referring to the mother who committed adultery
key_terms.حَقَّهَا: Her right (to claim the accusation against her son)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for accusing someone of their mother's adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle that the *hadd* for slander (*qadhf*) against a specific individual requires that person's presence to validate the claim and receive compensation, unless they are deceased. It highlights the distinction between the public aspect of the punishment and the private right (*haqq al-adam*) of the accused, emphasizing the mother's agency in confirming the accusation. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on procedural justice and the protection of individual honor in legal proceedings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5085 - Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Ammar Al-Sabati from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a man who said to another man, "O' son of an adulteress," intending adultery.

Imam (as) said: "If his mother is alive and present, and she comes forward to claim her right, the accuser is to be flogged eighty lashes.
If she is absent, it is to be delayed until she returns and claims her right.
And if she has passed away and nothing is known of her except goodness, the one who falsely accused her is to be given the legal punishment - eighty lashes."
